target.title: fix(chutes): validate OAuth redirect URI port is in range 1-65535
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/chutes/oauth.ts:68` calls `Number.parseInt(url.port, 10)` without validating the result is in the valid TCP port range 1-65535. The WHATWG URL parser accepts port 0 but strips ports > 65535, so a user providing `http://127.0.0.1:0/callback` as a redirect URI would get port 0 through to `waitForLocalOAuthCallback()`, potentially causing confusing failures.

This follows the zhangguiping-style input validation pattern: reject invalid values before they reach sensitive operations. See merged PRs #97133 (Nostr bounds check) and #96516 (reject invalid timeout).

## Changes

- `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`: add `Number.isFinite` + `1-65535` range check after `parseInt(url.port)`, throw descriptive Error on invalid port
- `extensions/chutes/oauth.test.ts`: export `parseRedirectUri` + 7 vitest tests covering default port, valid range (1, 1456, 65535), port 0 rejection, and stripped-port fallback

## Evidence

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/chutes/oauth.test.ts

 ✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts default port 80
 ✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts valid port 1456
 ✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts port 65535 (upper bound)
 ✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts port 1 (lower bound)
 ✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > rejects port 0
 ✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > defaults stripped port to 80
 ... (all 3 existing chutes OAuth tests pass)
```

Before: `parseRedirectUri("http://127.0.0.1:0/callback")` → `{ port: 0 }` (silently accepts invalid port)
After: `parseRedirectUri("http://127.0.0.1:0/callback")` → `Error: Chutes OAuth redirect URI port must be 1-65535 (got 0)`

Label: bugfix | merge-risk: 🟢 minimal | AI-assisted
